---
title: "C: Cardiovascular system"
description: "ATC group C for modelers: blood pressure and LDL as continuous surrogates, indirect response models, counter-regulation, and baseline as a trap."
date: "2026-02-08"
---

Drugs acting on the heart, the blood vessels and circulating lipids.
The large classes are developed against continuous biomarkers, blood pressure and LDL cholesterol [@kim2017fimasartan; @jadhav2023bempedoic], which is what makes dense exposure-response work practical here.

In July 1973, after screening thousands of fungal broths at Sankyo in Tokyo, Akira Endo isolated the first statin, ML-236B, from a *Penicillium citrinum* strain found on rice from a Kyoto grain shop [@endoHistoricalPerspectiveDiscovery2010].

|  | Description | In plain terms | Example drug |
| ---: | :--- | :--- | :--- |
| **C01** | Cardiac therapy | drugs acting directly on the heart | Amiodarone (C01BD01) / digoxin (C01AA05) |
| **C02** | Antihypertensives |  | Methyldopa (C02AB01), still standard in pregnancy / doxazosin (C02CA04), add-on in resistant hypertension. Note most first-line antihypertensives now sit in C03, C07, C08 and C09, not here. |
| **C03** | Diuretics |  | Furosemide (C03CA01) / spironolactone (C03DA01) |
| **C04** | Peripheral vasodilators | widen arteries in the arms and legs | Largely obsolete group; naftidrofuryl (C04AX21) is the only agent still guideline-recommended, for intermittent claudication. Pentoxifylline (C04AD03) is used but evidence is weak. |
| **C05** | Vasoprotectives | for hemorrhoids, varicose veins, fragile capillaries | Symptomatic only, with no single agent to name. The commonest are topical hydrocortisone (C05AA01) for hemorrhoids and oral diosmin (C05CA03) for chronic venous disease. |
| **C07** | Beta blocking agents |  | Bisoprolol (C07AB07) / metoprolol (C07AB02) |
| **C08** | Calcium channel blockers |  | Amlodipine (C08CA01) / diltiazem (C08DB01) |
| **C09** | Agents acting on the renin-angiotensin system | blood-pressure hormone system: ACE inhibitors, ARBs | Ramipril (C09AA05) / candesartan (C09CA06) |
| [**C10**](c10/) | Lipid modifying agents | cholesterol- and triglyceride-lowering drugs | Atorvastatin (C10AA05) / rosuvastatin (C10AA07) |

## Modeling notes

**Endpoint.**
Continuous surrogates measured repeatedly: blood pressure, LDL cholesterol [@bdwg2001biomarkers; @liaigre2025surrogacy].
Both lag plasma concentration, because the drug acts on the turnover of the measured quantity [@sharma1998indirect; @nicolas2019alirocumab].

**Typical structure.**
Indirect response models [@dayneka1993indirect; @jusko1994physiologic], near-universal for LDL [@kakara2014; @faltaos2006] and common for blood pressure.
Effect-compartment models only where the delay is genuinely short, as for the acute heart rate effect of a beta blocker [@francheteau1993; @belz1988].

**Counter-regulation (C02, C03, C09).**
Baroreflex activation, renin release and renal sodium handling push back against blood pressure effects [@sica2007], which is why feedback and tolerance terms appear in antihypertensive models [@brynne2001].

**Baseline is the trap.**
Blood pressure has a circadian rhythm, large measurement error and regression to the mean on enrolment [@hempel1998; @sumner1988], and placebo arms show genuine falls [@preston2000placebo; @patel2015placebo].
How baseline is handled changes bias and precision in the estimated drug effect, and normalising each observation by its own baseline is the worst common option [@dansirikul2008; @sun1999].

**Covariates worth pre-specifying.**
Renal function for diuretics and renally cleared renin-angiotensin agents [@hammarlund1989furosemide; @elungjensen2003enalapril], CYP2D6 for metoprolol and flecainide [@meloche2020cyp2d6; @thomas2020metoprolol], SLCO1B1 for statins [@turkmen2022slco1b1].
A data-driven search is underpowered at realistic dataset sizes [@ribbing2004covariate; @sanghavi2024covariate].

**Safety.**
A concentration-QTc analysis is expected under ICH E14 for essentially every new drug, as a separate pre-specified analysis [@garnett2018cqtc; @darpo2015iqcsrc] (see [C-QTc modeling](/docs/modeling/qt/)).
Class-matched effects such as hypotension and bradycardia are exaggerated on-target pharmacology, and keep climbing after the efficacy curve flattens [@johnston1992doseresponse; @overgaard2015er].

**Approval rests on the surrogate.**
Approval often rests on the surrogate, with the outcome trial reporting years later [@sabatine2017fourier; @nissen2023clear].
The pharmacometric job is linking biomarker change to event hazard [@holford2013tte; @zhudenkov2022joint], and handling the adherence and dropout endemic to chronic outpatient dosing [@vrijens2014adherence; @bjornsson2015dropout].
